analysis.title: Livin' on a Prayer: Whoa, We're Half Way There
key_insights: BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky notes the SPX made a high of 7844 in early October and trades near 7320, about 400 points lower. He sees risk to 7000, another roughly 400 points.
Small-caps, mid-caps, the Nasdaq, semis, industrials and transports are all below their 200-day moving averages (DMAs). Software had momentum this fall but failed, and IGV is back near its 200 DMA.
Krinsky says the oversold conditions of November 5 have been used up, so the market is in a weaker spot and a bounce is not the base case.
SPX is testing the 7250-7350 support zone for the fifth time since early June. His rule of thumb is that the more times a level is tested, the more likely it breaks.
BTIG expects SPX to break below its 200 DMA and fall at a minimum to the 7000-7100 zone.

AAPL (Not Rated) is called still vulnerable. It is a cyclical tech company, less exposed to AI and more defensive than semis, but a signal discussed on Sunday points to a high likelihood of materially lower prices over the coming weeks.
